title: Find Subarray With Bitwise OR Closest to K
summary: Given an array nums and an integer k, find a contiguous subarray whose bitwise OR of elements has the smallest absolute difference with k.
statement: Given an array nums and an integer k, find a contiguous subarray whose bitwise OR of elements has the smallest absolute difference with k. Return this minimum difference.
constraints: nums is a nonempty array of nonnegative integers and k is nonnegative.
Choose one nonempty contiguous subarray and compute the bitwise OR of all its values.
Return the minimum absolute difference between such an OR and k.
hints: For a fixed right endpoint, extending every prior subarray produces all ending OR values, and equal results may be deduplicated.
Carry the distinct OR set from the previous endpoint and OR every value with the new number.
current={number} union {old|number}; minimize abs(current-k); replace previous.
The recurrence represents every nonempty subarray by its unique left endpoint, while deduplication is safe because future OR extensions depend only on the current value.
editorial: The recurrence represents every nonempty subarray by its unique left endpoint, while deduplication is safe because future OR extensions depend only on the current value.

tests.explanation: The subarray [1,2] has bitwise OR three, so the minimum difference is zero.
Possible useful OR values include 8, 1, 2, and 3; value eight is closest with difference two.
